Transcript:
[53] Max Nightriver (player): I hold up the Guild badge so the archers can see it. We're from the Guild, the Sheridans sent us. Let us in before the sun's gone.
[54] Adolion Narrator: The lead archer leans on his bow and looks at the badge. "Guild-sent, are you?" He lowers his bow just an inch, but doesn't let it go completely. "The Sheridans finally heard us, is that it?" He looks at Belle and Dalan, then back at the badge. "If you're really Guild, then you've got the contract."
He narrows his eyes. "We're not opening the gate. We've got enough problems without adding more mouths to feed. But if you're really sent by the Guild and the Sheridans, you can get in by the north postern—the one by the pit-heads. We'll leave it unlocked for you. Just... don't say we didn't warn you."
He looks at you one more time, his eyes scanning your face. "And for the love of the gods, get in there before the sun goes down. Because after that, you'll wish we'd left the gate locked."
Then he turns back to the parapet and is silent.
What do you do?
[55] Max Nightriver (player): Thank you. And we have bandages for your wounded, if you have any. Come on, Ash Lanterns, round to the north postern by the pit-heads, quickly. I keep an eye on the sun.
[56] Dalan: Dalan's ears twitch at the mention of bandages, and he looks up with wide green eyes. "We have bandages," he repeats softly, and then his voice grows steady and determined. "And food. We have food and bandages."
He looks back at the archer, then to Max. "We should give them some. They sound like they need it." He looks back up at the parapet, his gaze scanning for anyone else, but finds none.
He adjusts the strap of his bow, and his looks at you. "I will help you. I have some bandages of my own. We can give them to the people on the wall."
He seems determined, and for the long moment, his gaze is unwavering.
Then he looks back at the road. "The pit-heads are north, yes? We should go."
His voice is quiet, but there is a quiet determination in it. "We should go now."
What do you do?*
[57] Max Nightriver (player): We lead the horse around the wall to the pit-heads and find the north postern. I try the door. If it opens, we slip inside and bar it behind us.
[58] Adolion Narrator: The pit-heads loom dark in the late-morning light, and the ground around them is hard and dry. The horse is restless in your hold, and the wind that blows through the trees is cold.
And then you find it—a small door in the wall, not quite high enough to be a proper gate. It is a simple wooden thing, and it sits in the shadow of the pit-head structure. And it is unlocked.
The door swings open with a soft creak, and the air that comes through it is cool and smells of damp earth and old stone.
And you step inside, and the door closes behind you. And the bar drops into place.
And you are inside Wendhope.
And it is silent.
The village is a narrow street that runs between timber-framed houses, and there is no sound and no smoke. And there are no people.
And there is only the sound of the wind, and the soft thud of the horse's hooves on the damp earth.
And the silence.
What do you do?*
[59] Max Nightriver (player): Inside, I look around for anyone at all. Hello? We're the Guild party. Belle, check the left side. Dalan, up high.
[60] Dalan: Dalan glances at the houses, his gaze sharp and scanning. "I... I see no movement," he repeats softly. He looks at you, a flicker of uncertainty crossing his face. "Not a single person. Not even in the windows." He adjusts the strap of his bow over his shoulder and looks back to the houses. "And not even the smoke of a fire. There is no reason for that."
He speaks in a low voice, but there is an uneasy edge to it. "We should find Mayor Douglas. If anyone knows what happened, it would be him."
His green eyes are wide and alert, and his posture is rigid. "But there is no one here. Nobody is moving."
He looks around again, and this time his gaze falls to a window. And he frowns. "Not even in the windows. There is no one looking out."
He looks back to Max, his expression grim. "Not even a single soul."
What do you do?*

[54] Adolion Narrator: The lead archer leans on his bow and looks at the badge. "Guild-sent, are you?" He lowers his bow just an inch, but doesn't let it go completely. "The Sheridans finally heard us, is that it?" He looks at Belle and Dalan, then back at the badge. "If you're really Guild, then you've got the contract."
He narrows his eyes. "We're not opening the gate. We've got enough problems without adding more mouths to feed. But if you're really sent by the Guild and the Sheridans, you can get in by the north postern—the one by the pit-heads. We'll leave it unlocked for you. Just... don't say we didn't warn you."
He looks at you one more time, his eyes scanning your face. "And for the love of the gods, get in there before the sun goes down. Because after that, you'll wish we'd left the gate locked."
Then he turns back to the parapet and is silent.
What do you do?
[55] Max Nightriver (player): Thank you. And we have bandages for your wounded, if you have any. Come on, Ash Lanterns, round to the north postern by the pit-heads, quickly. I keep an eye on the sun.
[56] Dalan: Dalan's ears twitch at the mention of bandages, and he looks up with wide green eyes. "We have bandages," he repeats softly, and then his voice grows steady and determined. "And food. We have food and bandages."
He looks back at the archer, then to Max. "We should give them some. They sound like they need it." He looks back up at the parapet, his gaze scanning for anyone else, but finds none.
He adjusts the strap of his bow, and his looks at you. "I will help you. I have some bandages of my own. We can give them to the people on the wall."
He seems determined, and for the long moment, his gaze is unwavering.
Then he looks back at the road. "The pit-heads are north, yes? We should go."
His voice is quiet, but there is a quiet determination in it. "We should go now."
What do you do?*
[57] Max Nightriver (player): We lead the horse around the wall to the pit-heads and find the north postern. I try the door. If it opens, we slip inside and bar it behind us.
[58] Adolion Narrator: The pit-heads loom dark in the late-morning light, and the ground around them is hard and dry. The horse is restless in your hold, and the wind that blows through the trees is cold.
And then you find it—a small door in the wall, not quite high enough to be a proper gate. It is a simple wooden thing, and it sits in the shadow of the pit-head structure. And it is unlocked.
The door swings open with a soft creak, and the air that comes through it is cool and smells of damp earth and old stone.
And you step inside, and the door closes behind you. And the bar drops into place.
And you are inside Wendhope.
And it is silent.
The village is a narrow street that runs between timber-framed houses, and there is no sound and no smoke. And there are no people.
And there is only the sound of the wind, and the soft thud of the horse's hooves on the damp earth.
And the silence.
What do you do?*
[59] Max Nightriver (player): Inside, I look around for anyone at all. Hello? We're the Guild party. Belle, check the left side. Dalan, up high.
[60] Dalan: Dalan glances at the houses, his gaze sharp and scanning. "I... I see no movement," he repeats softly. He looks at you, a flicker of uncertainty crossing his face. "Not a single person. Not even in the windows." He adjusts the strap of his bow over his shoulder and looks back to the houses. "And not even the smoke of a fire. There is no reason for that."
He speaks in a low voice, but there is an uneasy edge to it. "We should find Mayor Douglas. If anyone knows what happened, it would be him."
His green eyes are wide and alert, and his posture is rigid. "But there is no one here. Nobody is moving."
He looks around again, and this time his gaze falls to a window. And he frowns. "Not even in the windows. There is no one looking out."
He looks back to Max, his expression grim. "Not even a single soul."
What do you do?*

Transcript:
[54] Adolion Narrator: The lead archer leans on his bow and looks at the badge. "Guild-sent, are you?" He lowers his bow just an inch, but doesn't let it go completely. "The Sheridans finally heard us, is that it?" He looks at Belle and Dalan, then back at the badge. "If you're really Guild, then you've got the contract."
He narrows his eyes. "We're not opening the gate. We've got enough problems without adding more mouths to feed. But if you're really sent by the Guild and the Sheridans, you can get in by the north postern—the one by the pit-heads. We'll leave it unlocked for you. Just... don't say we didn't warn you."
He looks at you one more time, his eyes scanning your face. "And for the love of the gods, get in there before the sun goes down. Because after that, you'll wish we'd left the gate locked."
Then he turns back to the parapet and is silent.
What do you do?
[55] Max Nightriver (player): Thank you. And we have bandages for your wounded, if you have any. Come on, Ash Lanterns, round to the north postern by the pit-heads, quickly. I keep an eye on the sun.
[56] Dalan: Dalan's ears twitch at the mention of bandages, and he looks up with wide green eyes. "We have bandages," he repeats softly, and then his voice grows steady and determined. "And food. We have food and bandages."
He looks back at the archer, then to Max. "We should give them some. They sound like they need it." He looks back up at the parapet, his gaze scanning for anyone else, but finds none.
He adjusts the strap of his bow, and his looks at you. "I will help you. I have some bandages of my own. We can give them to the people on the wall."
He seems determined, and for the long moment, his gaze is unwavering.
Then he looks back at the road. "The pit-heads are north, yes? We should go."
His voice is quiet, but there is a quiet determination in it. "We should go now."
What do you do?*
[57] Max Nightriver (player): We lead the horse around the wall to the pit-heads and find the north postern. I try the door. If it opens, we slip inside and bar it behind us.
[58] Adolion Narrator: The pit-heads loom dark in the late-morning light, and the ground around them is hard and dry. The horse is restless in your hold, and the wind that blows through the trees is cold.
And then you find it—a small door in the wall, not quite high enough to be a proper gate. It is a simple wooden thing, and it sits in the shadow of the pit-head structure. And it is unlocked.
The door swings open with a soft creak, and the air that comes through it is cool and smells of damp earth and old stone.
And you step inside, and the door closes behind you. And the bar drops into place.
And you are inside Wendhope.
And it is silent.
The village is a narrow street that runs between timber-framed houses, and there is no sound and no smoke. And there are no people.
And there is only the sound of the wind, and the soft thud of the horse's hooves on the damp earth.
And the silence.
What do you do?*
[59] Max Nightriver (player): Inside, I look around for anyone at all. Hello? We're the Guild party. Belle, check the left side. Dalan, up high.
[60] Dalan: Dalan glances at the houses, his gaze sharp and scanning. "I... I see no movement," he repeats softly. He looks at you, a flicker of uncertainty crossing his face. "Not a single person. Not even in the windows." He adjusts the strap of his bow over his shoulder and looks back to the houses. "And not even the smoke of a fire. There is no reason for that."
He speaks in a low voice, but there is an uneasy edge to it. "We should find Mayor Douglas. If anyone knows what happened, it would be him."
His green eyes are wide and alert, and his posture is rigid. "But there is no one here. Nobody is moving."
He looks around again, and this time his gaze falls to a window. And he frowns. "Not even in the windows. There is no one looking out."
He looks back to Max, his expression grim. "Not even a single soul."
What do you do?*
[61] Belle: Belle doesn't wait for an order. She's already moving, her greataxe Cleaver in her hands and her brown eyes narrow and scanning the left side of the narrow street. "Check the left? I'm on it." She mutters, her voice low and rough. "Nobody's here, and nobody's hiding."
She walks along the buildings, her gaze flicking from window to window, and her hand tightens on the pommel of her greataxe. "No smoke, no sound, and no people. It's like a godsfucking hole in the world."
She looks back at you, her expression grim. "We're alone. And we're not alone. I can feel it."
Her brown eyes are hard, and her voice is low and sharp. "This place is wrong, and we're not leaving until we figure out what's wrong with it."
What do you do?*

[61] Belle: Belle doesn't wait for an order. She's already moving, her greataxe Cleaver in her hands and her brown eyes narrow and scanning the left side of the narrow street. "Check the left? I'm on it." She mutters, her voice low and rough. "Nobody's here, and nobody's hiding."
She walks along the buildings, her gaze flicking from window to window, and her hand tightens on the pommel of her greataxe. "No smoke, no sound, and no people. It's like a godsfucking hole in the world."
She looks back at you, her expression grim. "We're alone. And we're not alone. I can feel it."
Her brown eyes are hard, and her voice is low and sharp. "This place is wrong, and we're not leaving until we figure out what's wrong with it."
What do you do?*
[63] Adolion Narrator: The street is silent, and the windows are dark. And there is no movement on the walls. And the only sound is the wind, and the horse, and the creak of a board.
And the village is empty.
But the village is not dead.
And there is someone watching you from a window on the second floor of the house nearest the gate.
And they are silent. And they are watching you.
What do you do?*
[64] Max Nightriver (player): I climb the ladder to the parapet to find the archers who let us in. Who's in charge here, and what are you holding this wall against?
[65] Adolion Narrator: The ladder is simple wood, bolted to the inside of the wall. It rattles as you climb, and the stone of the parapet is cold beneath your boots.
Up top, there are three archers and one woman. The woman is an orc, tall and broad-shouldered with short-cropped black hair and red eyes. She is wearing a leather cuirass that has seen better days, and there is a longsword at her hip.
She is looking at the village below with an expression that is hard and weary.
She does not look at you as you approach.
"Who's in charge?" She says, her voice low and gravelly. "I am Captain Halena Vivinallo. And what we're holding this wall against is a lot of shit that hasn't killed us yet."
She turns to look at you then, her red eyes tracking your face. "Now tell me why you're here, Guild-sent. And tell me fast. We've got a lot to do before the sun goes down."
What do you do?*

[58] Adolion Narrator: The pit-heads loom dark in the late-morning light, and the ground around them is hard and dry. The horse is restless in your hold, and the wind that blows through the trees is cold.

The door swings open with a soft creak, and the air that comes through it is cool and smells of damp earth and old stone.
And you step inside, and the door closes behind you. And the bar drops into place.
And you are inside Wendhope.
And it is silent.
The village is a narrow street that runs between timber-framed houses, and there is no sound and no smoke. And there are no people.
And there is only the sound of the wind, and the soft thud of the horse's hooves on the damp earth.
And the silence.
What do you do?*

[60] Dalan: Dalan glances at the houses, his gaze sharp and scanning. "I... I see no movement," he repeats softly. He looks at you, a flicker of uncertainty crossing his face. "Not a single person. Not even in the windows." He adjusts the strap of his bow over his shoulder and looks back to the houses. "And not even the smoke of a fire. There is no reason for that."
He speaks in a low voice, but there is an uneasy edge to it. "We should find Mayor Douglas. If anyone knows what happened, it would be him."
His green eyes are wide and alert, and his posture is rigid. "But there is no one here. Nobody is moving."
He looks around again, and this time his gaze falls to a window. And he frowns. "Not even in the windows. There is no one looking out."
He looks back to Max, his expression grim. "Not even a single soul."
What do you do?*

Transcript:
[60] Dalan: Dalan glances at the houses, his gaze sharp and scanning. "I... I see no movement," he repeats softly. He looks at you, a flicker of uncertainty crossing his face. "Not a single person. Not even in the windows." He adjusts the strap of his bow over his shoulder and looks back to the houses. "And not even the smoke of a fire. There is no reason for that."
He speaks in a low voice, but there is an uneasy edge to it. "We should find Mayor Douglas. If anyone knows what happened, it would be him."
His green eyes are wide and alert, and his posture is rigid. "But there is no one here. Nobody is moving."
He looks around again, and this time his gaze falls to a window. And he frowns. "Not even in the windows. There is no one looking out."
He looks back to Max, his expression grim. "Not even a single soul."
What do you do?*
[61] Belle: Belle doesn't wait for an order. She's already moving, her greataxe Cleaver in her hands and her brown eyes narrow and scanning the left side of the narrow street. "Check the left? I'm on it." She mutters, her voice low and rough. "Nobody's here, and nobody's hiding."
She walks along the buildings, her gaze flicking from window to window, and her hand tightens on the pommel of her greataxe. "No smoke, no sound, and no people. It's like a godsfucking hole in the world."
She looks back at you, her expression grim. "We're alone. And we're not alone. I can feel it."
Her brown eyes are hard, and her voice is low and sharp. "This place is wrong, and we're not leaving until we figure out what's wrong with it."
What do you do?*
[63] Adolion Narrator: The street is silent, and the windows are dark. And there is no movement on the walls. And the only sound is the wind, and the horse, and the creak of a board.
And the village is empty.
But the village is not dead.
And there is someone watching you from a window on the second floor of the house nearest the gate.
And they are silent. And they are watching you.
What do you do?*
[64] Max Nightriver (player): I climb the ladder to the parapet to find the archers who let us in. Who's in charge here, and what are you holding this wall against?
[65] Adolion Narrator: The ladder is simple wood, bolted to the inside of the wall. It rattles as you climb, and the stone of the parapet is cold beneath your boots.
Up top, there are three archers and one woman. The woman is an orc, tall and broad-shouldered with short-cropped black hair and red eyes. She is wearing a leather cuirass that has seen better days, and there is a longsword at her hip.
She is looking at the village below with an expression that is hard and weary.
She does not look at you as you approach.
"Who's in charge?" She says, her voice low and gravelly. "I am Captain Halena Vivinallo. And what we're holding this wall against is a lot of shit that hasn't killed us yet."
She turns to look at you then, her red eyes tracking your face. "Now tell me why you're here, Guild-sent. And tell me fast. We've got a lot to do before the sun goes down."
What do you do?*
[66] Max Nightriver (player): The Sheridans hired the Guild to find out why the ore stopped. Looks like we found out. Put us to work, Captain. We hold the wall with you tonight. Belle, left side. Dalan, find a high spot.
[67] Dalan: Dalan hears the order and is already moving. "I will find a high point," he says softly, his voice clear and steady.
He adjusts the strap of his wooden longbow on his shoulder and glances back at you and Belle. "I... I will be ready."
He moves off toward the houses, his steps light and sure, his pointed ears alert. He is searching for a spot where he can see the village, and where he can get a good vantage point for his bow.
What do you do?*

[60] Dalan: Dalan glances at the houses, his gaze sharp and scanning. "I... I see no movement," he repeats softly. He looks at you, a flicker of uncertainty crossing his face. "Not a single person. Not even in the windows." He adjusts the strap of his bow over his shoulder and looks back to the houses. "And not even the smoke of a fire. There is no reason for that."
He speaks in a low voice, but there is an uneasy edge to it. "We should find Mayor Douglas. If anyone knows what happened, it would be him."
His green eyes are wide and alert, and his posture is rigid. "But there is no one here. Nobody is moving."
He looks around again, and this time his gaze falls to a window. And he frowns. "Not even in the windows. There is no one looking out."
He looks back to Max, his expression grim. "Not even a single soul."
What do you do?*
[61] Belle: Belle doesn't wait for an order. She's already moving, her greataxe Cleaver in her hands and her brown eyes narrow and scanning the left side of the narrow street. "Check the left? I'm on it." She mutters, her voice low and rough. "Nobody's here, and nobody's hiding."
She walks along the buildings, her gaze flicking from window to window, and her hand tightens on the pommel of her greataxe. "No smoke, no sound, and no people. It's like a godsfucking hole in the world."
She looks back at you, her expression grim. "We're alone. And we're not alone. I can feel it."
Her brown eyes are hard, and her voice is low and sharp. "This place is wrong, and we're not leaving until we figure out what's wrong with it."
What do you do?*
[63] Adolion Narrator: The street is silent, and the windows are dark. And there is no movement on the walls. And the only sound is the wind, and the horse, and the creak of a board.

And there is someone watching you from a window on the second floor of the house nearest the gate.
And they are silent. And they are watching you.
What do you do?*

Up top, there are three archers and one woman. The woman is an orc, tall and broad-shouldered with short-cropped black hair and red eyes. She is wearing a leather cuirass that has seen better days, and there is a longsword at her hip.
She is looking at the village below with an expression that is hard and weary.
She does not look at you as you approach.
"Who's in charge?" She says, her voice low and gravelly. "I am Captain Halena Vivinallo. And what we're holding this wall against is a lot of shit that hasn't killed us yet."

Transcript:
[61] Belle: Belle doesn't wait for an order. She's already moving, her greataxe Cleaver in her hands and her brown eyes narrow and scanning the left side of the narrow street. "Check the left? I'm on it." She mutters, her voice low and rough. "Nobody's here, and nobody's hiding."
She walks along the buildings, her gaze flicking from window to window, and her hand tightens on the pommel of her greataxe. "No smoke, no sound, and no people. It's like a godsfucking hole in the world."
She looks back at you, her expression grim. "We're alone. And we're not alone. I can feel it."
Her brown eyes are hard, and her voice is low and sharp. "This place is wrong, and we're not leaving until we figure out what's wrong with it."
What do you do?*
[63] Adolion Narrator: The street is silent, and the windows are dark. And there is no movement on the walls. And the only sound is the wind, and the horse, and the creak of a board.
And the village is empty.
But the village is not dead.
And there is someone watching you from a window on the second floor of the house nearest the gate.
And they are silent. And they are watching you.
What do you do?*
[64] Max Nightriver (player): I climb the ladder to the parapet to find the archers who let us in. Who's in charge here, and what are you holding this wall against?
[65] Adolion Narrator: The ladder is simple wood, bolted to the inside of the wall. It rattles as you climb, and the stone of the parapet is cold beneath your boots.
Up top, there are three archers and one woman. The woman is an orc, tall and broad-shouldered with short-cropped black hair and red eyes. She is wearing a leather cuirass that has seen better days, and there is a longsword at her hip.
She is looking at the village below with an expression that is hard and weary.
She does not look at you as you approach.
"Who's in charge?" She says, her voice low and gravelly. "I am Captain Halena Vivinallo. And what we're holding this wall against is a lot of shit that hasn't killed us yet."
She turns to look at you then, her red eyes tracking your face. "Now tell me why you're here, Guild-sent. And tell me fast. We've got a lot to do before the sun goes down."
What do you do?*
[66] Max Nightriver (player): The Sheridans hired the Guild to find out why the ore stopped. Looks like we found out. Put us to work, Captain. We hold the wall with you tonight. Belle, left side. Dalan, find a high spot.
[67] Dalan: Dalan hears the order and is already moving. "I will find a high point," he says softly, his voice clear and steady.
He adjusts the strap of his wooden longbow on his shoulder and glances back at you and Belle. "I... I will be ready."
He moves off toward the houses, his steps light and sure, his pointed ears alert. He is searching for a spot where he can see the village, and where he can get a good vantage point for his bow.
What do you do?*
[Scene direction: The first night on Wendhope's walls. The red fog rolls in from Needlehaven. The Screechers arrive. Make them scary. Give a moment to Belle, Max, Dalan. Show how they react and how they fight. Make them fragile: wounded but fragile. Some die. They bubble and fade. The fog thins by dawn.]
[68] Adolion Narrator: The sun is still high in the sky, but there is a chill in the air, and the forest is quiet around you.
The orc Captain looks at the party for a long moment, her red eyes hard and calculating. Then she nods, once, and turns back to the village below. "You're all right."
She gestures to one of the archers, who is sitting on a stone bench, and points to a pile of crates near the center of the wall walk. "You're all on the watch. And if anything comes out of those trees, you shoot it. And you don't stop until it's dead."
And then she looks at you one more time. "And you'll wish you'd taken the posting."
And the wind picks up, and it carries with it the faint scent of pine and old earth, and the sun begins to set.
What do you do?*

Transcript:
[61] Belle: Belle doesn't wait for an order. She's already moving, her greataxe Cleaver in her hands and her brown eyes narrow and scanning the left side of the narrow street. "Check the left? I'm on it." She mutters, her voice low and rough. "Nobody's here, and nobody's hiding."
She walks along the buildings, her gaze flicking from window to window, and her hand tightens on the pommel of her greataxe. "No smoke, no sound, and no people. It's like a godsfucking hole in the world."
She looks back at you, her expression grim. "We're alone. And we're not alone. I can feel it."
Her brown eyes are hard, and her voice is low and sharp. "This place is wrong, and we're not leaving until we figure out what's wrong with it."
What do you do?*
[63] Adolion Narrator: The street is silent, and the windows are dark. And there is no movement on the walls. And the only sound is the wind, and the horse, and the creak of a board.
And the village is empty.
But the village is not dead.
And there is someone watching you from a window on the second floor of the house nearest the gate.
And they are silent. And they are watching you.
What do you do?*
[64] Max Nightriver (player): I climb the ladder to the parapet to find the archers who let us in. Who's in charge here, and what are you holding this wall against?
[65] Adolion Narrator: The ladder is simple wood, bolted to the inside of the wall. It rattles as you climb, and the stone of the parapet is cold beneath your boots.
Up top, there are three archers and one woman. The woman is an orc, tall and broad-shouldered with short-cropped black hair and red eyes. She is wearing a leather cuirass that has seen better days, and there is a longsword at her hip.
She is looking at the village below with an expression that is hard and weary.
She does not look at you as you approach.
"Who's in charge?" She says, her voice low and gravelly. "I am Captain Halena Vivinallo. And what we're holding this wall against is a lot of shit that hasn't killed us yet."
She turns to look at you then, her red eyes tracking your face. "Now tell me why you're here, Guild-sent. And tell me fast. We've got a lot to do before the sun goes down."
What do you do?*
[66] Max Nightriver (player): The Sheridans hired the Guild to find out why the ore stopped. Looks like we found out. Put us to work, Captain. We hold the wall with you tonight. Belle, left side. Dalan, find a high spot.
[67] Dalan: Dalan hears the order and is already moving. "I will find a high point," he says softly, his voice clear and steady.
He adjusts the strap of his wooden longbow on his shoulder and glances back at you and Belle. "I... I will be ready."
He moves off toward the houses, his steps light and sure, his pointed ears alert. He is searching for a spot where he can see the village, and where he can get a good vantage point for his bow.
What do you do?*
[Scene direction: The first night on Wendhope's walls. The red fog rolls in from Needlehaven. The Screechers arrive. Make them scary. Give a moment to Belle, Max, Dalan. Show how they react and how they fight. Make them fragile: wounded but fragile. Some die. They bubble and fade. The fog thins by dawn.]
[68] Adolion Narrator: The sun is still high in the sky, but there is a chill in the air, and the forest is quiet around you.
The orc Captain looks at the party for a long moment, her red eyes hard and calculating. Then she nods, once, and turns back to the village below. "You're all right."
She gestures to one of the archers, who is sitting on a stone bench, and points to a pile of crates near the center of the wall walk. "You're all on the watch. And if anything comes out of those trees, you shoot it. And you don't stop until it's dead."
And then she looks at you one more time. "And you'll wish you'd taken the posting."
And the wind picks up, and it carries with it the faint scent of pine and old earth, and the sun begins to set.
What do you do?*

Transcript:
[63] Adolion Narrator: The street is silent, and the windows are dark. And there is no movement on the walls. And the only sound is the wind, and the horse, and the creak of a board.
And the village is empty.
But the village is not dead.
And there is someone watching you from a window on the second floor of the house nearest the gate.
And they are silent. And they are watching you.
What do you do?*
[64] Max Nightriver (player): I climb the ladder to the parapet to find the archers who let us in. Who's in charge here, and what are you holding this wall against?
[65] Adolion Narrator: The ladder is simple wood, bolted to the inside of the wall. It rattles as you climb, and the stone of the parapet is cold beneath your boots.
Up top, there are three archers and one woman. The woman is an orc, tall and broad-shouldered with short-cropped black hair and red eyes. She is wearing a leather cuirass that has seen better days, and there is a longsword at her hip.
She is looking at the village below with an expression that is hard and weary.
She does not look at you as you approach.
"Who's in charge?" She says, her voice low and gravelly. "I am Captain Halena Vivinallo. And what we're holding this wall against is a lot of shit that hasn't killed us yet."
She turns to look at you then, her red eyes tracking your face. "Now tell me why you're here, Guild-sent. And tell me fast. We've got a lot to do before the sun goes down."
What do you do?*
[66] Max Nightriver (player): The Sheridans hired the Guild to find out why the ore stopped. Looks like we found out. Put us to work, Captain. We hold the wall with you tonight. Belle, left side. Dalan, find a high spot.
[67] Dalan: Dalan hears the order and is already moving. "I will find a high point," he says softly, his voice clear and steady.
He adjusts the strap of his wooden longbow on his shoulder and glances back at you and Belle. "I... I will be ready."
He moves off toward the houses, his steps light and sure, his pointed ears alert. He is searching for a spot where he can see the village, and where he can get a good vantage point for his bow.
What do you do?*
[Scene direction: The first night on Wendhope's walls. The red fog rolls in from Needlehaven. The Screechers arrive. Make them scary. Give a moment to Belle, Max, Dalan. Show how they react and how they fight. Make them fragile: wounded but fragile. Some die. They bubble and fade. The fog thins by dawn.]
[68] Adolion Narrator: The sun is still high in the sky, but there is a chill in the air, and the forest is quiet around you.
The orc Captain looks at the party for a long moment, her red eyes hard and calculating. Then she nods, once, and turns back to the village below. "You're all right."
She gestures to one of the archers, who is sitting on a stone bench, and points to a pile of crates near the center of the wall walk. "You're all on the watch. And if anything comes out of those trees, you shoot it. And you don't stop until it's dead."
And then she looks at you one more time. "And you'll wish you'd taken the posting."
And the wind picks up, and it carries with it the faint scent of pine and old earth, and the sun begins to set.
What do you do?*
[69] Belle: Belle does not hesitate. She's already moving, her greataxe Cleaver in her hands and her brown eyes scanning the forest. "Left side," she mutters, her voice low and rough. "I'll hold it."
She walks to the edge of the wall, her grip tightening on the pommel of Cleaver as she looks out over the trees. "And I hope this party has any fucking teeth."
Her brown eyes are hard, and she's looking at the forest with an expression that is grim and focused.
What do you do?*

beats.objective: Travel the north road toward Wendhope and let the party notice what the road is missing: no ore wagons, no peddlers, no patrols, no smoke on the horizon, and a growing absence of birdsong as the forest edge nears.
beats.guidance: Play the road as a long, quiet stretch of world pressure. The Ash Lanterns are three days out of Aegis City with rope, lanterns, and a week of rations. Let the party choose their pace, their camp, and what they investigate. Dalan can read the forest and notice the silence first; Belle can push for speed or challenge the quiet; Max can reason about the Sheridans' missing ore. The world does not wait: the further north they go, the more the road shows its neglect. A waystation is abandoned, its firepit cold for weeks. A milestone is scratched over with a crude spiral. No one passes them in either direction. If they camp, the first night is windless and watchful. If they push on, they reach the last rise before Wendhope by dusk. Either way, the road itself is the warning.

beats.objective: Reach the walls of Wendhope before sundown and find the gate shut, barred, and guarded by frightened villagers who refuse entry to strangers as night falls.
beats.guidance: The party arrives at Wendhope as the sun drops behind the treeline. The palisade is intact but hastily reinforced with fresh-cut timber and wagon parts. The gate is closed. Figures on the wall watch the forest, not the road. When the party approaches, a voice calls down: 'Hold, Wendhope is closed.' The villagers will not open for just anyone. They have been besieged every night for weeks and have lost people who were let in after dark. Let the party negotiate, present the Guild posting, invoke the Sheridans, or find another way in. The world presses: the sun is going down, the forest is going quiet, and something in the trees is already moving. If the party is still outside when the last light fails, the first assault begins with them on the wrong side of the wall.

entries.text: Max Nightriver approached Tobias at the Guild counter in Aegis City and asked about the high-paying Wendhope posting, learning it was an investigation into a silent mining village that no party had claimed for three days. Max recruited Belle, a bored barbarian, and Dalan Evergreen, a shy elven ranger, to form a party, and Tobias warned them to prepare properly for the danger. At the counter, Ellie registered them as the Ash Lanterns, and the newly formed party set out through the north gate to buy supplies before heading to Wendhope.
entries.evidence:
Max Nightriver: We'll buy rope and lanterns on the way out. Ellie, you've had that pen ready all morning. Put us down as the Ash Lanterns.
Ellie: Ellie's eyebrows rise slightly, and she sets her pen down with a measured click. "The Ash Lanterns," she repeats softly, her blue eyes flicking between the three of you, as if trying to picture it. "That is a fine name." A small, genuine smile touches her lips before she picks up her pen again and writes it in the Guild's register. "The Ash Lanterns, taking the Wendhope investigation." Her handwriting is elegant and precise. "You're all F-rank, so your rewards will be D-rank standard, plus the Sheridan travel stipend." She pauses, then looks up at you. "We'll have that ready for you when you return. I hope to see you all again."
Max Nightriver: Thank you, Ellie. Right, Ash Lanterns: market for rope, lanterns and a week of rations, then the north gate before noon.
Belle: Belle pushes off from the tavern arch, and for the moment, the grin has vanished from her face. She looks at the party—at Max, at Dalan—with brown eyes that seem to be sizing them up as if they were a pack of hounds. "Right. Rations, rope, and lanterns. We'll pick those up as we go. The north gate is far." She looks at you, her hand resting on Cleaver's pommel. "And I hope this party has any fucking teeth."
Adolion Narrator: The Guild hall is loud enough to be heard from the street, and the scent of old wax and stale ale hangs in the air. Outside, the north gate is a long way off, and the street is busy with the bustle of Aegis City's morning market.
You have formally taken the Wendhope posting as the Ash Lanterns—F-rank, but with a D-rank reward and travel stipend to claim. The sun is high, and the road north is open.
Belle walks ahead, her greataxe’s weight easy on her shoulder. Dalan follows, his wooden longbow still, his eyes quiet and watchful.
What do you do?
Max Nightriver: Once we're past the city fields I fall in beside Dalan. So, a year between parties. What went wrong with the last ones?
Dalan: Dalan's ears twitch, and he looks up with wide green eyes, surprised that anyone is talking to him. He seems to hesitate for a moment, his hand gripping the strap of his bow.
"I... I have not had many parties," he admits softly, his gaze falling to the path. "They did not... they did not want me. They said I was not strong enough. That I was too soft to fight." He looks back at Max, a flicker of something passing through his expression. "They did not see me shoot."
His voice is quiet, but there is a quiet determination in it. "I have been registered for a year. I have not yet had a chance to prove myself."

entries.text: Max Nightriver found a riderless Sheridan-blue horse on an empty road and led it north with Belle and Dalan, unsettled by the absence of traffic. They discovered an overturned merchant carriage with no bodies, blood, or tracks, so they camped beside it through a silent night. At dawn they left the carriage as found and pushed on to Wendhope, which they found silent and still.
entries.evidence:
Max Nightriver: I catch the horse's bridle and check the saddlebags. Sheridan blue. Belle, Dalan, look at this. Where's the rider?
Belle: Belle's brown eyes narrow as she looks at the horse, her gaze travelling slowly from the saddle to the riderless bridle in your hand. She shifts her weight, her hand moving to the pommel of Cleaver. "Sheridan blue," she mutters, her voice rough like grinding stones. "Somebody's missing their horse. Or their rider's missing something." She looks at you with a hard, searching expression. "Where'd you find it? On the road?"
Max Nightriver: It walked down the road to us, Belle. I lead it along with us; the Sheridans will want it back. We keep moving north. Anyone else notice there's no traffic on this road?
Belle: Belle's gaze flickers over the road, her expression grim as she takes in the absence of any travellers. "Traffic? I noticed we ain't seen a single soul for miles. No merchants, no farmers, not even a shitting dog." She looks at the road again, her hand tightening on Cleaver's pommel. "Something's wrong. I can feel it in my gut, and my gut's usually right." She looks at you, her brown eyes hard. "You notice it too, don't you?"
Adolion Narrator: Dalan has fallen silent, his green eyes scanning the treeline and the road ahead. The horse walks beside the group, its hooves muffled by the road's damp earth. The wind has shifted, carrying with it the faint scent of pine and damp earth.
Further north, where the road bends through the trees, there is a flash of something that catches the eye—a gleam of polished metal in the distance, half obscured by the pines.
Max Nightriver: I notice it too. I raise a hand to halt us and squint at the gleam in the pines. Dalan, your eyes are better than mine. What is that?
Dalan: Dalan steps forward, his pointed ears twitching as his gaze fixes on the distance. He narrows his eyes, and for a long moment, he is silent. His face is still, but his eyes are sharp, and his posture is rigid.
Then, he speaks, his voice low and measured. "It is metal. Polished metal, and it is moving. It is... it is a carriage."
He looks at you, a flicker of uncertainty crossing his face. "It is overturned on its side. And there are no people near it."
Max Nightriver: We approach carefully, Belle in front, Dalan with an arrow nocked. I ready a ward spell and look over the carriages for tracks, blood, anything.
Adolion Narrator: The overturned carriage lies on its side in a shallow ditch, one of its wheels still spinning slowly in the air. Its side is painted with the crest of a merchant house — a golden scale over a field of blue. The cargo, still strapped to the roof, is a collection of heavy wooden crates.
The ground around the carriage is churned up, but there are no clear signs of a fight. No blood on the grass. No arrow shafts in the trees. And no bodies.
Just the silence. And the wind that smells of old pines and damp earth.
Belle's hand is white-knuckled on the pommel of Cleaver, and Dalan's arrow is nocked, his bowstring taut. He is scanning the treeline with a sharp, alert gaze.
What do you do?
Max Nightriver: No bodies, no blood. That's worse. It's getting dark; we make camp by the carriages and keep a watch. I'll take first watch, Belle second, Dalan the dawn.
Dalan: Dalan lowers his bow just a little, the arrow still nocked but his posture relaxing. "No blood," he echoes softly, and his voice carries a hint of uncertainty. "That is... not natural." He looks at Max, his green eyes searching. "A monster would leave a mess. And bandits... they would have taken the cargo."
He looks back at the carriage, then to the forest that surrounds them. "You think the people are still alive?"
Adolion Narrator: The wind picks up as dusk settles over the clearing, and the light is turning amber. The trees are shadows and the road is a dark ribbon between them. The horse is restless in your hold.
Belle says, "No blood doesn't mean nothing." She is standing with her greataxe in hand, her eyes scanning the forest around them. "Maybe they were taken. Alive." Her voice is hard, and her brown eyes are dark. "We'll keep a watch. That's a good idea."
She looks at you, her expression grim. "You take the first watch. I'll be second. Dalan gets the dawn." She gives a short, sharp nod and looks to the forest. "And if anything comes out of those trees, we'll be ready."
Max Nightriver: Maybe. Whoever they are, they didn't run from bandits. I build a small fire in the lee of the carriage, tie the Sheridan horse close, and settle in for first watch.
Adolion Narrator: The fire is small and controlled, and its light is barely enough to keep the darkness away. The Sheridan horse is quiet, its hooves softly shifting in the dirt. The forest is silent around you, and the wind that blows through the trees is cold and carries the scent of pine and old earth.
Belle and Dalan retreat into the shadows for the rest of the evening. Belle lies with her greataxe beside her, and Dalan curls into a ball under his green cloak, his bow within reach.
The watch is long. And the forest is still.
The horse is quiet. And the fire is dying.
But the road is still there, and the carriage is still there, and there is no sign of anyone coming.
The only sound is the crackle of the fire, and the distant howl of a wolf or something like it, and the soft shift of the horse’s hooves.
What do you do?
Max Nightriver: The night passes without anyone coming. At dawn we break camp, leave the carriage as we found it, and push hard north for Wendhope.
Adolion Narrator: The dawn comes with a chill, and the air is thick with mist. Dalan stirs first, and Belle is already awake, her hand resting on the pommel of Cleaver. They look at the overturned carriage, and then at you, and then at the road that lies ahead.
The road is empty, and the mists are thick, and the horse is still quiet.
"We leave it," Belle says, her voice low and rough. "We leave it as we found it. And we push on."
She looks at the horse, then back at the road. "Wendhope is far. We'll need to get there before the sun gets too high."
The party moves out, and the horse follows, its hooves soft on the damp earth. The mists part as the sun rises, and the forest thins as the road leads you north.
And then, after another hour of travel, you come to a ridge overlooking a valley. And there, in the distance, you see it.
A stone wall, a ring of houses, and the pit-heads and ore carts of a mining village.
Wendhope.
It sits in the valley, and there is no smoke from the fires, and there are no people in the streets. And there is nothing that moves, or shifts, or stirs, in the quiet of the morning.

entries.text: Max Nightriver led the party down the ridge road to the village gate, where they found the settlement silent and empty, with no smoke, no movement, and no answer to his knock. Dalan reported seeing no one on the wall walk, while Belle readied her greataxe and warned that something unnatural was at work. The group stood at the gate unsettled, surrounded by wind, silence, and the sense that they were not alone.
entries.evidence:
Max Nightriver: No smoke at breakfast time. I don't like it. We go down the ridge road to the village gate, slow, weapons ready but not drawn.
Adolion Narrator: The village is still. And the horse is still. And the people are still.
The ridge road is steep, and the slope is rocky, and the descent is slow. The village gate is a simple wooden thing, and the stone wall around the village is low, and there is a ring of timber-framed houses.
And there is nobody in the streets.
The stone-and-timber houses are shut, and the windows are dark, and there is no sound in the village. And there is no smoke in the sky.
Belle's greataxe is in her hand, and she is close to you. Dalan's bow is in his hand, and he is close to him.
And you are in the center of it all.
The only sound in the village is the wind, and the soft thud of the horse's hooves.
And the silence.
What do you do?
Max Nightriver: I walk up to the gate and knock, loud. Hello the gate! Guild party from Aegis, sent by the Sheridans. Is anyone in there?
Adolion Narrator: Your knock is loud, and it echoes through the village, and the sound is flat and sharp. But there is no answer.
And there is no movement.
And there is no one who comes to the gate, and there is no voice that replies, and there is no hand that opens it.
There is only the silence, and the wind, and the soft shifting of the horse's hooves, and the look on Belle's face.
Her brown eyes are hard, and her hand is tightening on the pommel of her greataxe.
What do you do?
Max Nightriver: I step back and look up at the wall walk. Dalan, do you see anyone up there? I call out again: we have food and bandages, we only want to talk.
Dalan: Dalan steps forward beside Max, and his pointed ears twitch as he glances up at the wall. His eyes are wide and focused, and for a long moment, he is silent. Then he speaks, his voice low and soft.
"I... I see nothing," he admits, his gaze scanning the battlements again and again. "Nobody is moving up there." He looks back at Max, a flicker of uncertainty crossing his face. "Is that possible? That a whole village is just... empty?"
Belle: Belle's brown eyes narrow and she looks at the empty road. "A whole village empty? Fuck that." She spits on the ground and looks at the gate. "Something is wrong. And it ain't natural." She looks back at Dalan. "Get your bow ready. I can't shake the feeling that we're not alone out here."
Adolion Narrator: The wind is cold and carries the scent of pine and damp earth, and the forest is silent around you. The village sits in the valley below, and there is no smoke from the fires, and there is nothing moving in the streets.
And there is only the sound of your voice, and the knock, and the silence that follows.
And there is the horse, and the carriage, and the empty road, and the absence of people.
The only movement in the village is the fluttering of a tattered cloth tied to one of the buildings, and the distant rustle of leaves in the wind.
And the horse is quiet. And the silence is thick.
What do you do?

entries.text: Max Nightriver and the Ash Lanterns arrived at the silent village of Wendhope after finding unsettling signs on the road, including an empty Sheridan-blue horse and an abandoned merchant carriage. When three archers on the parapet warned them to turn back before sundown, Max showed his Guild badge and the lead archer directed them to enter through the north postern by the pit-heads. After Dalan Evergreen offered bandages and food, the party led the horse around the wall, found the unlocked postern, and slipped inside, barring the door behind them to face the village's unnatural silence.
entries.evidence:
Max Nightriver: (OOC: Narrator, I've been away a day. Can you give me a quick summary of where we are and what's going on?)
Adolion Narrator: The Ash Lanterns—your party of three—just took a D-rank posting from the Adventurer's Guild in Aegis City to investigate a silent mining village called Wendhope in the Sheridan lands. You're Max Nightriver, a noble-born mage, joined by Belle, a barbarian with a greataxe, and Dalan Evergreen, an elven ranger.
You've just arrived at Wendhope after traveling north for a day and finding some unsettling signs along the way: an empty Sheridan-blue horse you kept and are still leading, and an overturned merchant carriage with no bodies, no blood, and no signs of a struggle—just missing people.
The village itself is silent, no smoke, no movement, no one in the streets, which feels unnatural. You tried knocking and calling out for the villagers, but for a while, no one responded.
Then, three archers finally appeared on the wall parapet. The lead archer, who has a scar over his eye and looks exhausted, has warned you to turn back now or not make it to the crossroads before sundown—implying that whatever is happening in Wendhope makes it dangerous to linger until dark.
Belle and Dalan are with you, and the archers are staring you down with arrows nocked.
What do you do?
Max Nightriver: I hold up the Guild badge so the archers can see it. We're from the Guild, the Sheridans sent us. Let us in before the sun's gone.
Adolion Narrator: The lead archer leans on his bow and looks at the badge. "Guild-sent, are you?" He lowers his bow just an inch, but doesn't let it go completely. "The Sheridans finally heard us, is that it?" He looks at Belle and Dalan, then back at the badge. "If you're really Guild, then you've got the contract."
He narrows his eyes. "We're not opening the gate. We've got enough problems without adding more mouths to feed. But if you're really sent by the Guild and the Sheridans, you can get in by the north postern—the one by the pit-heads. We'll leave it unlocked for you. Just... don't say we didn't warn you."
He looks at you one more time, his eyes scanning your face. "And for the love of the gods, get in there before the sun goes down. Because after that, you'll wish we'd left the gate locked."
Then he turns back to the parapet and is silent.
What do you do?
Max Nightriver: Thank you. And we have bandages for your wounded, if you have any. Come on, Ash Lanterns, round to the north postern by the pit-heads, quickly. I keep an eye on the sun.
Dalan: Dalan's ears twitch at the mention of bandages, and he looks up with wide green eyes. "We have bandages," he repeats softly, and then his voice grows steady and determined. "And food. We have food and bandages."
He looks back at the archer, then to Max. "We should give them some. They sound like they need it." He looks back up at the parapet, his gaze scanning for anyone else, but finds none.
He adjusts the strap of his bow, and his looks at you. "I will help you. I have some bandages of my own. We can give them to the people on the wall."
He seems determined, and for the long moment, his gaze is unwavering.
Then he looks back at the road. "The pit-heads are north, yes? We should go."
His voice is quiet, but there is a quiet determination in it. "We should go now."
What do you do?*
Max Nightriver: We lead the horse around the wall to the pit-heads and find the north postern. I try the door. If it opens, we slip inside and bar it behind us.
Adolion Narrator: The pit-heads loom dark in the late-morning light, and the ground around them is hard and dry. The horse is restless in your hold, and the wind that blows through the trees is cold.
And then you find it—a small door in the wall, not quite high enough to be a proper gate. It is a simple wooden thing, and it sits in the shadow of the pit-head structure. And it is unlocked.
The door swings open with a soft creak, and the air that comes through it is cool and smells of damp earth and old stone.
And you step inside, and the door closes behind you. And the bar drops into place.
And you are inside Wendhope.
And it is silent.
The village is a narrow street that runs between timber-framed houses, and there is no sound and no smoke. And there are no people.
And there is only the sound of the wind, and the soft thud of the horse's hooves on the damp earth.
And the silence.
What do you do?*

Adolion Narrator: The ladder is simple wood, bolted to the inside of the wall. It rattles as you climb, and the stone of the parapet is cold beneath your boots.
Up top, there are three archers and one woman. The woman is an orc, tall and broad-shouldered with short-cropped black hair and red eyes. She is wearing a leather cuirass that has seen better days, and there is a longsword at her hip.
She is looking at the village below with an expression that is hard and weary.
She does not look at you as you approach.
"Who's in charge?" She says, her voice low and gravelly. "I am Captain Halena Vivinallo. And what we're holding this wall against is a lot of shit that hasn't killed us yet."
She turns to look at you then, her red eyes tracking your face. "Now tell me why you're here, Guild-sent. And tell me fast. We've got a lot to do before the sun goes down."
What do you do?*

canon.text:
WHAT HAS HAPPENED:
Max Nightriver, a noble-born mage of House Nightriver, signed the Adventurers' Guild register three days earlier with a new badge, a light purse, and no party. The Wendhope posting—an investigation of the village, not a clearing of it, paid for by the Sheridans over ore that had stopped coming—sat unclaimed because no party would take it. Dalan Evergreen, a shy elf Ranger with a wooden longbow who had been registered for a year without finding a party, and Belle, who wielded a stone-headed greataxe named Cleaver and intended to fight on the front line, joined Max to form a party, since the Guild sent no one out alone. Belle proposed the arrangement: she would take the front line, Dalan would take the shots, and Max would handle the rest. She demanded to know how much coin the journey to Wendhope would cost before agreeing. With the terms settled, Max named the party the Ash Lanterns, and Ellie wrote the name into the Guild register, formally taking the Wendhope investigation and allowing the Guild to hand over the posting. Tobias advised the party to bring rope, lanterns, a week of rations, a second exit for every room, and a priest who can bless the dead. Max planned to buy rope, lanterns, and a week of rations at the market, then reach the north gate before noon.

CURRENT STATE:
The party of three—Max, Belle, and Dalan—is committed to the Wendhope posting and is traveling north on the road to Wendhope. The story's current checkpoint is the road north, where the party is to notice what the road is missing. The party holds F-rank, so their rewards will be D-rank standard plus the Sheridan travel stipend, which Ellie will have ready when the party returns. The party plans to buy rope and lanterns on the way out of the city. The Wendhope job remains an investigation of the village rather than a clearing of it, and the Sheridans are paying for the ore that stopped coming.

ESTABLISHED FACTS:
The Wendhope job is listed as investigate the village, not clear it out. The Sheridans are paying for the ore that stopped coming from Wendhope. Dalan Evergreen is a Ranger who wields a wooden longbow. Belle wields a greataxe named Cleaver, a stone-headed weapon, and will take the front line. removed.text: Max Nightriver approached Tobias at the Guild counter and asked what work paid well without getting the party killed. Tobias pointed him toward the Wendhope posting, warning that it read like a collapsed mine and was too risky for an unproven party. When Max pressed about the catch, Tobias explained the Sheridans were paying for the missing ore, but the job was only to investigate why the village had gone silent, and it had sat unclaimed for three days. Max then recruited Belle, a bored barbarian with a greataxe named Cleaver, and Dalan Evergreen, a shy elf Ranger who had been guild-registered for a year without a party. Belle agreed once Max noted the Sheridans covered travel, and the three settled into roles: Belle on the front line, Dalan on ranged support, and Max handling the rest. They now need to formally take the posting at the counter, where Ellie will ask for a party name.
removed.evidence:
Adolion Narrator: You came to Aegis City to make a name with a blade, a bow or a spell, and three days ago you signed the Adventurers' Guild register to do it. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall is loud enough to be heard from the street. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.

What do you do?
Max Nightriver: I wander over to the counter and nod at Tobias. What's on the board that pays and won't get us killed?
Tobias: Tobias straightens from the board, ocean eyes tracking you with the quiet scrutiny of one who has seen too many green-badged adventurers go out thinking they will return. "The board is full of work that pays. It is the question of whether you wish to pay for it with coin or with blood." He gestures with a slender finger towards the notice he had been tapping. "The Wendhope posting is high-pay, as is the Sheridan fee. But it reads like a collapsed mine shaft. I would not recommend it to an unproven party." He pauses, hesitating. "Would you have a better idea of what you would like to do?"
Max Nightriver: Tobias, what's the catch with the Wendhope posting? Nobody pays that much for a collapsed mine.
Tobias: Tobias's ocean blue eyes flicker with something—perhaps a brief, uneasy flash of concern, or maybe just the flicker of a pale, cautious curiosity. He hesitates for a moment before leaning a little closer across the counter.
"Indeed, they do not. Which is why it has been posted for three days without a single party taking it." He taps the paper, the ink still fresh. "The Sheridans are paying for the ore that stopped coming. But this job—it is listed as *investigate* the village and find out what happened, not clear it out. There is a difference between a cave-in and something that made the people stop talking altogether."
He draws back, his expression returning to its usual stoic calm. "The Guild is not in the business of sending people to their deaths. But if a party chooses to take it, we will not stop them. The risk is high, but the rewards are higher still."
Max Nightriver: I turn toward the tavern arch. Belle, Dalan, you two look about as bored as I am. Investigating a quiet village sounds better than rat-catching. Want to make a party of it?
Belle: Belle does not move from the tavern arch, her brown eyes narrow and calculating as she studies the stranger who has dared to approach her. "A party, he says," she mutters, her voice low and rough like grinding stones. "Better than rat-catching, sure enough. But Wendhope is far as fuck." She looks him over, from boots to pauldrons, and for a moment it seems as like she is sizing him up as if he were a piece of meat.
Then, a slow grin spreads across her face, all teeth. "You got any idea how much coin that will cost us to get there?"
Max Nightriver: The Sheridans pay the travel, Belle, it's in the posting. Dalan? You've been reading the same notice for ten minutes. Bow, sword and axe. Sounds like a party to me.
Dalan: Dalan's pointed ears twitch at the sound of his name, and he glances up from the posting with wide, green eyes. A small, pink blush colours his cheeks as he shifts his weight from one foot to the other, and he seems to hesitate.
"I... I suppose so," he says, his voice soft and polite. "I have been registered at the Guild for a year now, but I have not yet found a party that... that is." He trails off, his eyes darting between the stranger and Belle, and then back to the and notice. "If you wish to take the posting, I would be happy to join you." He seems almost nervous, but there is a light in his eyes—a quiet determination that betrays a his shyness.
He adjusts the strap of his wooden longbow over his shoulder and looks back at the stranger. "My name is Dalan Evergreen. I am a Ranger."
Belle: Belle's eyes flick between the elf and the stranger, and then she gives a short, sharp laugh. "A Ranger and a... what are you, then?" She asks the stranger, her hand resting on the pommel of Cleaver's stone head. "We're taking the posting, then. I'll handle the front line. Ranger gets the shots. You do the rest." She looks back at them, her grin widening. "Now let's see if this party's got any fucking teeth."
Max Nightriver: (OOC: Narrator, I'm new to this. What should I do next?)
Adolion Narrator: You have gathered a party for a D-rank posting: investigate the silent village of Wendhope in the Sheridan lands to find out why ore stopped arriving. You have agreed with your party-mates: Belle will take the front line with her greataxe Cleaver, and Dalan Evergreen will provide ranged support with his longbow. You need to take this posting formally at the counter.
This is your chance to show Belle and Dalan what kind of teammate you are. You might ask them about themselves, discuss your equipment and preparations for the trip, or plan what you can do on the journey there. You are a noble-born mage from House Nightriver—is that who you will show them, or something else?
Or you could walk straight to the counter where Ellie and Tobias will handle your registration and hand you the posting. If you do do that, Ellie will ask you for a party name.
What would you like to do?

Adolion Narrator: Dalan has fallen silent, his green eyes scanning the treeline and the road ahead. The horse walks beside the group, its hooves muffled by the road's damp earth. The wind has shifted, carrying with it the faint scent of pine and damp earth.
Further north, where the road bends through the trees, there is a flash of something that catches the eye—a gleam of polished metal in the distance, half obscured by the pines.
Max Nightriver: I notice it too. I raise a hand to halt us and squint at the gleam in the pines. Dalan, your eyes are better than mine. What is that?
Dalan: Dalan steps forward, his pointed ears twitching as his gaze fixes on the distance. He narrows his eyes, and for a long moment, he is silent. His face is still, but his eyes are sharp, and his posture is rigid.
Then, he speaks, his voice low and measured. "It is metal. Polished metal, and it is moving. It is... it is a carriage."
He looks at you, a flicker of uncertainty crossing his face. "It is overturned on its side. And there are no people near it."
Max Nightriver: We approach carefully, Belle in front, Dalan with an arrow nocked. I ready a ward spell and look over the carriages for tracks, blood, anything.
Adolion Narrator: The overturned carriage lies on its side in a shallow ditch, one of its wheels still spinning slowly in the air. Its side is painted with the crest of a merchant house — a golden scale over a field of blue. The cargo, still strapped to the roof, is a collection of heavy wooden crates.
The ground around the carriage is churned up, but there are no clear signs of a fight. No blood on the grass. No arrow shafts in the trees. And no bodies.
Just the silence. And the wind that smells of old pines and damp earth.
Belle's hand is white-knuckled on the pommel of Cleaver, and Dalan's arrow is nocked, his bowstring taut. He is scanning the treeline with a sharp, alert gaze.
What do you do?
Max Nightriver: No bodies, no blood. That's worse. It's getting dark; we make camp by the carriages and keep a watch. I'll take first watch, Belle second, Dalan the dawn.
Dalan: Dalan lowers his bow just a little, the arrow still nocked but his posture relaxing. "No blood," he echoes softly, and his voice carries a hint of uncertainty. "That is... not natural." He looks at Max, his green eyes searching. "A monster would leave a mess. And bandits... they would have taken the cargo."
He looks back at the carriage, then to the forest that surrounds them. "You think the people are still alive?"
Adolion Narrator: The wind picks up as dusk settles over the clearing, and the light is turning amber. The trees are shadows and the road is a dark ribbon between them. The horse is restless in your hold.
Belle says, "No blood doesn't mean nothing." She is standing with her greataxe in hand, her eyes scanning the forest around them. "Maybe they were taken. Alive." Her voice is hard, and her brown eyes are dark. "We'll keep a watch. That's a good idea."
She looks at you, her expression grim. "You take the first watch. I'll be second. Dalan gets the dawn." She gives a short, sharp nod and looks to the forest. "And if anything comes out of those trees, we'll be ready."
Max Nightriver: Maybe. Whoever they are, they didn't run from bandits. I build a small fire in the lee of the carriage, tie the Sheridan horse close, and settle in for first watch.
Adolion Narrator: The fire is small and controlled, and its light is barely enough to keep the darkness away. The Sheridan horse is quiet, its hooves softly shifting in the dirt. The forest is silent around you, and the wind that blows through the trees is cold and carries the scent of pine and old earth.
Belle and Dalan retreat into the shadows for the rest of the evening. Belle lies with her greataxe beside her, and Dalan curls into a ball under his green cloak, his bow within reach.
The watch is long. And the forest is still.
The horse is quiet. And the fire is dying.
But the road is still there, and the carriage is still there, and there is no sign of anyone coming.
The only sound is the crackle of the fire, and the distant howl of a wolf or something like it, and the soft shift of the horse’s hooves.
What do you do?

Max Nightriver: The night passes without anyone coming. At dawn we break camp, leave the carriage as we found it, and push hard north for Wendhope.
Adolion Narrator: The dawn comes with a chill, and the air is thick with mist. Dalan stirs first, and Belle is already awake, her hand resting on the pommel of Cleaver. They look at the overturned carriage, and then at you, and then at the road that lies ahead.
The road is empty, and the mists are thick, and the horse is still quiet.
"We leave it," Belle says, her voice low and rough. "We leave it as we found it. And we push on."
She looks at the horse, then back at the road. "Wendhope is far. We'll need to get there before the sun gets too high."
The party moves out, and the horse follows, its hooves soft on the damp earth. The mists part as the sun rises, and the forest thins as the road leads you north.
And then, after another hour of travel, you come to a ridge overlooking a valley. And there, in the distance, you see it.
A stone wall, a ring of houses, and the pit-heads and ore carts of a mining village.
Wendhope.
It sits in the valley, and there is no smoke from the fires, and there are no people in the streets. And there is nothing that moves, or shifts, or stirs, in the quiet of the morning.
What do you do?
Max Nightriver: No smoke at breakfast time. I don't like it. We go down the ridge road to the village gate, slow, weapons ready but not drawn.
Adolion Narrator: The village is still. And the horse is still. And the people are still.
The ridge road is steep, and the slope is rocky, and the descent is slow. The village gate is a simple wooden thing, and the stone wall around the village is low, and there is a ring of timber-framed houses.
And there is nobody in the streets.
The stone-and-timber houses are shut, and the windows are dark, and there is no sound in the village. And there is no smoke in the sky.
Belle's greataxe is in her hand, and she is close to you. Dalan's bow is in his hand, and he is close to him.
And you are in the center of it all.
The only sound in the village is the wind, and the soft thud of the horse's hooves.
And the silence.
What do you do?
Max Nightriver: I walk up to the gate and knock, loud. Hello the gate! Guild party from Aegis, sent by the Sheridans. Is anyone in there?
Adolion Narrator: Your knock is loud, and it echoes through the village, and the sound is flat and sharp. But there is no answer.
And there is no movement.
And there is no one who comes to the gate, and there is no voice that replies, and there is no hand that opens it.
There is only the silence, and the wind, and the soft shifting of the horse's hooves, and the look on Belle's face.
Her brown eyes are hard, and her hand is tightening on the pommel of her greataxe.
What do you do?
Max Nightriver: I step back and look up at the wall walk. Dalan, do you see anyone up there? I call out again: we have food and bandages, we only want to talk.
Dalan: Dalan steps forward beside Max, and his pointed ears twitch as he glances up at the wall. His eyes are wide and focused, and for a long moment, he is silent. Then he speaks, his voice low and soft.
"I... I see nothing," he admits, his gaze scanning the battlements again and again. "Nobody is moving up there." He looks back at Max, a flicker of uncertainty crossing his face. "Is that possible? That a whole village is just... empty?"
Belle: Belle's brown eyes narrow and she looks at the empty road. "A whole village empty? Fuck that." She spits on the ground and looks at the gate. "Something is wrong. And it ain't natural." She looks back at Dalan. "Get your bow ready. I can't shake the feeling that we're not alone out here."
Adolion Narrator: The wind is cold and carries the scent of pine and damp earth, and the forest is silent around you. The village sits in the valley below, and there is no smoke from the fires, and there is nothing moving in the streets.
And there is only the sound of your voice, and the knock, and the silence that follows.
And there is the horse, and the carriage, and the empty road, and the absence of people.
The only movement in the village is the fluttering of a tattered cloth tied to one of the buildings, and the distant rustle of leaves in the wind.
And the horse is quiet. And the silence is thick.
What do you do?
Adolion Narrator: Three bows come up on the parapet at once. "That's far enough!" The archer in the middle has a scar over his left eye and has not slept in days. "Wendhope's not taking visitors. Turn round now and you'll make the crossroads by sundown."
Max Nightriver: (OOC: Narrator, I've been away a day. Can you give me a quick summary of where we are and what's going on?)
Adolion Narrator: The Ash Lanterns—your party of three—just took a D-rank posting from the Adventurer's Guild in Aegis City to investigate a silent mining village called Wendhope in the Sheridan lands. You're Max Nightriver, a noble-born mage, joined by Belle, a barbarian with a greataxe, and Dalan Evergreen, an elven ranger.
You've just arrived at Wendhope after traveling north for a day and finding some unsettling signs along the way: an empty Sheridan-blue horse you kept and are still leading, and an overturned merchant carriage with no bodies, no blood, and no signs of a struggle—just missing people.
The village itself is silent, no smoke, no movement, no one in the streets, which feels unnatural. You tried knocking and calling out for the villagers, but for a while, no one responded.
Then, three archers finally appeared on the wall parapet. The lead archer, who has a scar over his eye and looks exhausted, has warned you to turn back now or not make it to the crossroads before sundown—implying that whatever is happening in Wendhope makes it dangerous to linger until dark.
Belle and Dalan are with you, and the archers are staring you down with arrows nocked.
What do you do?

WHAT HAS HAPPENED:
